q: What training window does the current monthly churn-xgb retrain use?
a: The latest 9 observation months of cards.churn_labels, per the 2026-10-30 decision; churn-xgb-v3 itself was fit on 2025-01 to 2025-09.

q: Which churn models depend on feat-utilization-v1, and what did the 2026-10-29 check mean for them?
a: churn-xgb-v2 and churn-xgb-v3 both use feat-utilization-v1; the 2026-10-29 check found no post-period days in its three util_ columns, so it stays unchanged in v3.

q: What came of the exp-017 leak check run on 2026-10-28?
a: Removing post-period days took AUC from 0.81 to 0.74; the finding was followed on 2026-10-29 by the post-period-leak conclusion that the velocity aggregation leaks the target, and on 2026-10-30 Sam Lee decided to rebuild velocity as feat-velocity-v3 and retire v2.

q: How was the holdout-2025q4 evaluation set built, and when was it frozen?
a: A random 30% of accounts, stratified by tenure band, with Oct-Dec 2025 observation dates (1.2M accounts) and never used for training; frozen 2026-09-04, split by nb/make_holdout.ipynb.

q: What AUC and recall@10 did the logistic baseline reach on holdout-2025q4, and what was n and the feature count?
a: AUC 0.71 and recall@10 0.29 on holdout-2025q4, n=1.2M, with 14 account-level features (no velocity or utilization), reported 2026-09-15.

q: Why is recall@10 used to judge decisions rather than AUC?
a: Retention can call only 10% of the book each month, so the question is how many 90-day churners land in the top 10% of scores; AUC is reported alongside but decisions use recall@10.

q: Which velocity feature version is current, and how does its window differ from v2?
a: feat-velocity-v3, decided 2026-10-30, supersedes v2 and keeps the same 6 vel_ columns, but its window is the 30 days before the observation date, where v2 used the 30 days around it.

q: What does feat-velocity-v3 read from, and which model uses it?
a: It reads cards.txn_daily (code features/velocity_v3.py) and builds 6 vel_ columns from the 30 days before the observation date plus their ratio to the prior 90-day average; churn-xgb-v3 uses it.

q: What did the 2026-10-26 leak review start from, and where did its September data question end up?
a: It began a review of the exp-014 velocity columns and the team asked data-eng-cards about the short September partitions; the September backfill of cards.txn_daily (ticket DE-4411) finished on 2026-10-27.

q: How is the 90-day churn label in cards.churn_labels defined, and who maintains it?
a: It is a 90-day churn flag per account and month-end observation date: the account has no card spend for the 90 days after the observation date. The retention-labels job builds it from cards.txn_daily, and data-eng-cards maintains it.
